value.produces: amix-system.hdf golden master (AMIX 2.1 OPEN LOOK desktop; cold-boot reset)

labctl.notes: HOST-NATIVE: FS-UAE 3.2.35 (its OWN copy at assets/amix/fsuae-native, built with FSUAE_STATION=amix) runs an Amiga 3000 (68030+MMU, Kickstart 2.04 r37.175) on the host inside a pinned Xvfb sized to the emulator window; the daemon captures the X root (SH_CAPTURE=x11) and injects input over XTEST. No QEMU/QMP, no exec channel. POINTER IS OPEN: the daemon injects absolute XTEST motion (the x11test contract), but the GUEST tracks it relatively and with acceleration — the UAE mousehack that gives amigaos35 a 1:1 pointer is an AmigaOS trap, and AMIX drives the Amiga mouse hardware itself. Measured on the sandbox rig: host (160,120)->guest ~(82,92), host (480,380)->guest ~(331,345), history-dependent. The tile stays hidden until this is closed (an x11test-rel daemon backend, or FS-UAE grab-mode calibration). Reset=relaunch: cold boot (~2 min) of a fresh work HDF copied from disk/amix-system.hdf.golden; no statefile. Launcher stations/amix/x11-runtime.sh.

render.stationsManifestPrelude: # amix — host-native FS-UAE 3.2.35 (A3000, 68030+MMU, Kickstart 2.04) -> Amiga UNIX (AMIX) 2.1, System V R4 with the OPEN LOOK desktop. Ships monochrome 640x512 today (AMIX's Amiga-chipset X server is depth 1); colour OPEN LOOK on the A2410 (1024x768, 8-bit) is proven on this same binary and its golden awaits promotion (docs/guests/amix.md).

listing.reason: Dark launch: the pointer is not 1:1 yet (docs/guests/amix.md), and the operator's call is open on monochrome-vs-A2410 colour. Promote by dropping this block once both are closed.

museum.lineage: Commodore Amiga / UNIX System V Release 4 (AT&T, ported by Commodore)
eraSoftware: the OPEN LOOK File Manager and Calculator
museum.periodBrowser: none — 1992 predates the web reaching Unix desktops; AMIX shipped uucp, cnews and an SVR4 TCP/IP stack instead
museum.blurb: Commodore shipped a real AT&T System V Release 4 for the Amiga 3000 — and put OPEN LOOK on it, not Motif. Almost nobody bought an A3000UX, so almost nobody has seen this running: a Sun-styled Unix desktop booting off a 68030 that was supposed to be selling Workbench.
museum.notes: Live streamhost tile, HOST-NATIVE from birth: FS-UAE 3.2.35 on the host under a pinned Xvfb, x11 root capture + XTEST input, with its own copy of the binary (rule 6). Installed from real media — the AMIX 2.1 boot/root floppies and the 29-segment installation tape (amigaunix.com) restored through UAE's SCSI tape emulation onto a 2 GB RDB disk, exactly as a real A3000UX did it. The desktop is MONOCHROME 640x512 because AMIX's Amiga-chipset X server is depth 1; colour needs an A2410 (or Resolver/1600GX) board, and FS-UAE 3.2.35 compiles the A2410 code but never calls it. Distinct from amiga (A500/WB1.3), amigaos35 (A4000/OS 3.5) and aros. See docs/guests/amix.md.

network.note: No networking. AMIX ships an SVR4 TCP/IP stack and FS-UAE emulates the A2065 Ethernet card the A3000UX used, so a retronet web-plane join is a real follow-up; it is deliberately out of scope for the first landing, and the install declined the hosts-file step.

reset.mouse: OPEN — guest tracks XTEST motion RELATIVELY and with acceleration, not 1:1; see docs/guests/amix.md "The pointer is not 1:1". Keyboard is unaffected.
reset.fixture: AMIX 2.1 OPEN LOOK desktop on a 640x512 monochrome screen: an xterm titled 'Amiga UNIX 2.1' showing 'UNIX_System_V amix 4.0 2.1 0800430 Amiga (Unlimited) m68k' over a root shell, the OPEN LOOK Calculator, and xclock. Started from /etc/inittab (entry 'xw', run level 2) via xinit /etc/kh-xsession, so the desktop is up without a login. resetMode=relaunch with no statefile: reset is a COLD BOOT (~2 min to the desktop) of a fresh work HDF copied from disk/amix-system.hdf.golden. BAKE RULE: halt the guest with /sbin/shutdown -y -g0 -i0 before copying the golden — UFS has no host-repairable dirty flag, and a golden taken from a killed emulator makes every visitor's boot run a full fsck (~4 min instead of ~2). Keyboard PASS on the sandbox rig 2026-08-30 (XTEST). Mouse OPEN: motion reaches the guest but is relative and accelerated.
